cells.tense: You are at the part of the work where the understanding is done and all that is left is to say it plainly.
cells.ask: Put the finished thing in front of one person today, whole, and let their reading of it stand without your corrections.
cells.core:
Your thinking on this one has run its course. Nothing is left to work out — the shape is settled, and you can hold it without needing another pass at it. That is what becoming what you are looks like in the mind: the whole thing shows at once and you do not have to keep checking it.

What you are free to feed from here is more thinking of the same quality — patterns seen cleanly, useful, no strain in them. So let the next piece sit in front of someone else and be read back to you. You will find out where your own clarity is strongest by watching which parts survive being handled.
cells.sheetLine: Your understanding here has finished, and you can say it plainly.
cells.verb: seeing a thing through to its end
cells.place: where what you are stops being held back

cells.tense: You are bracing for a future moment when you will finally be clear enough, and you are spending the present rehearsing for it.
cells.ask: Pick the smallest piece you can finish today, finish it, then set it down and go do something with your hands.
cells.core:
You are pushing past the end. The understanding on this has arrived, and you keep testing it, sharpening it, checking whether it is really as clear as it seems — as if one more turn of the screw would make it certain. At its best, this settles and you trust it. Right now the screw keeps turning.

The pushing costs you the ease the understanding was for. What is open instead is fresher ground — something you know nothing about yet. Try a thing badly on purpose, ask a question you cannot answer, let a beginner's hour happen. The clarity you are guarding will hold without the guard duty.
cells.sheetLine: You keep polishing a thing that is already clear enough.

cells.tense: The understanding finished and you are living as though the last step were still ahead of you.
cells.ask: Say one sentence of what you figured out to the next person who asks how it is going, before you have planned it.
cells.core:
You worked something out and then went quiet about it. The conclusion is sitting in a drawer while you wait for a better moment to bring it out — a moment that keeps not arriving. There is no penalty left to avoid, and showing what you are does not require the timing to be perfect.

The thing to do is small: let one person hear the finished version, roughly, today. Not a summary, not a defence of it — just the conclusion, spoken to someone who can take it. What you settled is closer to being lived once it has been said out loud.

cells.tense: You are the one doing the turning here, and you keep describing it as something that happens to you.
cells.ask: Name one thing you called luck or timing today and say out loud what you actually did to bring it about.
cells.core:
The shift is already underway and you are not crediting yourself for it. You keep saying the timing was right, the pieces fell into place, the moment arrived — as though the figuring out were done by someone else. It was done by you, in each small choice of what to look at and what to let go.

Start marking that. Take one hour from today that went the way you wanted and trace what you did. Nothing grand — the choice of a word, the thing you let pass. The light is already on. It just needs your name on the switch.
cells.sheetLine: You keep calling your own turning point good timing.

attempts.check: The record makes Clarity the completion of a process of understanding, and the seat is becoming what you are through knowing — it does not support the idea that the completion has to happen before the expressing can be allowed. A reader who is still mid-process could reasonably say this card has nothing to do with them; the ask survives because the doing happens before the seeing is finished, which is true for anyone who keeps holding the draft. The sentence that would serve me more than them is any line where I get to be the one who already sees — the whole thing is written so the seeing belongs to whoever is sitting there.
